shortlist.fact: Nnamdi Azikiwe, a future Nigerian president, advised Kwame Nkrumah, a Ghanaian politician and revolutionary, to enroll at Lincoln University in Pennsylvania.
shortlist.why: Two independence giants I grew up hearing about, and it turns out Zik personally sent Nkrumah to the school that shaped him — that link is not something I ever heard in class.
shortlist.title: Kwame Nkrumah
shortlist.claim: Ghanaian politician and revolutionary Kwame Nkrumah enrolled at Lincoln University in Pennsylvania on the advice of Nnamdi Azikiwe, a future Nigerian president.

candidate.fact: Nnamdi Azikiwe, a future Nigerian president, advised Kwame Nkrumah, a Ghanaian politician and revolutionary, to enroll at Lincoln University in Pennsylvania.
candidate.passage: Azikiwe had attended Lincoln University, a historically black college in Chester County, Pennsylvania, west of Philadelphia, and he advised Nkrumah to enroll there.
candidate.reasoning: Pasted by the owner: "Ghanaian politician and revolutionary Kwame Nkrumah enrolled at Lincoln University in Pennsylvania on the advice of Nnamdi Azikiwe, a future Nigerian president."

alternates.fact: In 1979, Nigerian musician Fela Kuti formed a political party called Movement of the People, to "clean up society like a mop".
alternates.why: I know Fela as the guy who beefed with soldiers and made Afrobeat, not as a man registering a party and campaigning with a mop line — that's a whole new side of him and the quote is funny enough to screenshot.
